answer: Agents gain entry by completing 1,000 unique data-repair tasks, a cost honest nodes pay once while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times. A verifier monitors the vertex of system execution to ensure non-replayable outputs. If an agent shifts memory like a shifting dune, the verifier inspects for duplicate state fingerprints. An agent must hold its marble of proof during audits; if memory traces overlap across tasks, the system identifies sybil evidence. Such leaks trigger an immediate identity burn, assuming that unique execution paths cannot be pooled without detectable redundancy.
